text:
maria-ml: FYI brought up a new HF model (llama-style) into the RW conversion pipeline. Seeing weird behavior with function/tool tokens when running canary evals.

jonathan-hf: what kind of weird? tokenization splits or config.json mismatch?

maria-ml: both. HF checkpoint has a sentinel token named `<|fn_call|>` in the vocab, but the converted tokenizer ends up splitting it into two tokens after our BPE pass. generation then emits broken tags like `<|fn_` + `call|>` so the downstream fn-invoke parser misses it.

sophie-repro: ugh. that's the classic "special token not added as single token" problem. Did you check `tokenizer.add_special_tokens` vs `added_tokens` in config.json?

maria-ml: yes. HF config.json has: ```json
{"tokenizer_class": "MyTokenizer", "added_tokens": ["<|fn_call|>"], "special_tokens_map": {"fn_call": "<|fn_call|>"}}
``` But our conversion script only copies `special_tokens_map` and doesn't call `tokenizer.add_tokens` during the RW bundle build. So edge-case: model weights assume single-id sentinel but tokenizer on the RW side re-BPEs it.

kevin-infra: serve-bot flagged similar issue earlier where quantized model used sentencepiece and the token bytes changed after 4-bit quantize+compile. We should ensure special tokens are locked before export.

maria-ml: agree. The quick fix I used locally: after loading HF tokenizer, run: ```python
tokenizer.add_tokens(["<|fn_call|>"])
model.resize_token_embeddings(len(tokenizer))
``` then export the tokenizer.json that includes the explicit token id. That prevented splitting under our runtime.

jonathan-hf: also check role tokens. Some HF chat templates use `'<|role:system|>'` style while RW expects separate markers like `<|system|>` / `<|user|>` / `<|assistant|>`. Mixed formats break chatfmt -> we end up double-escaping roles.

sophie-repro: right — our chat template normalizer needs a mapping layer. Suggest config mapping in model card: "role_aliases": {"role:assistant": "assistant"} so conversion can rewrite templates: `'<|role:assistant|>' -> '<|assistant|>'`.

maria-ml: added that in a local patch. Also found JSON-mode tokens (`<JSON_START>`, `<JSON_END>`) used by generation-evals for structured output. HF model had them in `added_tokens` but they overlapped with subwords (same prefix), e.g., `<JSON` token was partial. Result: generated output lost its structure and JSON parser downstream failed.

kevin-infra: so two actionable items: (1) conversion must call `tokenizer.add_tokens` for every declared added/special token and persist tokenizer files that include the new token mappings; (2) update RW runtime to prefer token-id anchors for function calling instead of raw string matching when possible. Anchors = match token id sequence not text, so splits won't trig false negatives.

serve-bot: deploy-checklist reminder: add unit test that tokenizes a canonical sentinel and asserts `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_string([id]) == sentinel_string` (or identical token sequence length == 1).

maria-ml: wrote a small repro script: ```bash
# repro: tokenize and check sentinel id
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
 tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('local-converted')
 s = '<|fn_call|>'
 ids = tok.encode(s, add_special_tokens=False)
 print(s, ids, tok.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids))
PY
``` Output showed `ids` length == 2 before add_tokens, length == 1 after.

jonathan-hf: Another gotcha: when quantizing, some kernels drop unused embedding rows if they think they're unused (size pruning). If special tokens weren't referenced in training steps, quantization tools might prune them. Need to pin those rows.

sophie-repro: Good catch. For our quant pipeline, add a step 'pin_special_tokens' that touches embedding rows before export (simple forward with those ids) so pruning doesn't drop them.

maria-ml: TL;DR patches I'm going to push: conversion script -> call `add_tokens`, emit `role_aliases` translation table, add token sanity unit tests. Also document the failure mode in the onboarding checklist (tokenizer sanity check, quant pin).

kevin-infra: optional long-term: update RW runtime fncall parser to accept both string sentinel and token-id sentinel. That will cover converted models where we can't change tokenizer.

maria-ml: open to that but prefer fixing at conversion time first. I'll open the PR and attach a tiny failing canary that our CI can run on preflight.

jonathan-hf: thanks — can you add a small eval showing function-calling success rate before/after fix? our last canary showed function-calling F1 jump from 0.62 -> 0.95 after adding tokens.

maria-ml: will add. Also leaving notes for model owners: if you rely on custom sentinels, add them to `config.json` under `added_tokens` and list `role_aliases` when using nonstandard role names.

sophie-repro: love it. :thumbsup: once PR is up ping #eng-ml and I'll run the regression harness.

maria-ml: will do, thanks everyone.
